title: Stop Double-Booked Appointments
description: A clinic booking service on PostgreSQL (default read committed) checks whether a slot has an appointment and, if not, inserts one. Under load, a few slots end up with two appointments. What is the most reliable fix?

options.text: Add a UNIQUE constraint on appointments(slot_id) and return "slot taken" when the insert violates it.
options.explanation: The database checks the constraint at commit for every interleaving, so only one booking per slot can ever succeed, regardless of isolation level.

options.text: Switch the transactions to repeatable read.
options.explanation: PostgreSQL repeatable read is snapshot isolation. Both transactions see no appointment and insert different new rows, so no write conflict is detected and both can commit.

options.text: Cache slot availability in Redis with a short TTL and check it before inserting.
options.explanation: A cache read is another check-then-act on possibly stale data; it narrows nothing and adds a second source of truth.

options.text: Retry failed bookings with exponential backoff.
options.explanation: The double-booked transactions did not fail, so there is nothing to retry. Retries do not create mutual exclusion.
